title: Python SDK: streaming validators and retry hooks for structured outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a streaming-first validation and retry integration for the Python SDK that makes typed model hydration resilient, low-latency, and retry-safe. Goal is to provide developers ergonomic helpers for: 1) incremental validation of streaming chunks against Pydantic/dataclass schemas, 2) a retry-aware stream iterator that can resume without duplicating emitted items, and 3) compatibility helpers that provide deterministic fallbacks when schema evolution occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming iterator API: developers can iterate over responses as typed objects (Pydantic or dataclass) and the iterator exposes a .resume(token_id) primitive to resume from a safe replay point.
Partial validation: chunk-by-chunk validation runs in O(chunk_size) with an option to switch between 'strict' (fail on first mismatch) and 'tolerant' (emit placeholder/warning + telemetry) modes.
Retry hooks: when the SDK retries a request, it does not re-emit already-delivered typed objects to callers; documented semantics for idempotency keys and rehydration of KV cache are included.
Compatibility helpers: utilities to auto-coerce renamed fields and provide migration hints when Pydantic schema mismatches occur; unit tests cover at least three schema-evolution scenarios.

Examples: add a cookbook example showing (a) streaming chat messages hydrated to dataclasses with backpressure handling, (b) a long-running streaming embed flow that resumes after transient network failure, and (c) integration test against the hosted API with a flaky network simulator.
technical_notes: Design: introduce StreamModel[T] typing wrapper that accepts either a Pydantic model class or dataclass type and returns an async iterator that yields validated T instances as they become available.

Validation strategy: run fast permissive checks on every chunk (type coercion, missing optional fields) and schedule a full strict pass on the assembled object for users who opt into synchronous validation. This reduces tail latency for common cases.

Retry semantics: attach deterministic "stream-offset" tokens to each yielded object. On retry, the server/SDK agree on a resume token; SDK resumes by skipping previously-yielded offsets. For local-only retries (client-side reconnects), we replay from last confirmed offset to avoid duplicates.
Backpressure: iterator exposes .pause()/.resume() for consumer-driven buffering; internal queue defaults to a small bounded buffer and exposes metrics (queue_len, avg_latency).

Pydantic vs dataclasses: provide a thin adapter that uses Pydantic BaseModel.parse_obj for validation and a dataclass path that uses dacite-like conversion + optional runtime type checks. Keep adapters pluggable to allow 3rd-party validators.

Performance: microbenchmarks suggest per-chunk parse/validate adds ~0.3-0.8ms on typical model payloads (100-300 bytes) when using pydantic v2. Provide a config knob to disable validation in hot paths.

Telemetry: emit structured events for validation failures (fields, reason, chunk_id), retry/resume events (from_offset, to_offset), and buffering/backpressure alerts. Tag telemetry with customer_id when available.
Security: schema migration helpers must avoid executing arbitrary code during coercion. All coercion rules are declarative; any custom coercion requires an explicit developer-provided callable.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete—implemented prototype StreamModel wrapper and measured baseline overhead. Prototype repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pulls/1423 (draft).
2026-03-04: Design review with SDK and Runtime teams. Decided on offset-token format (64bit monotonically increasing per-request) and approach for client-side replay vs server resume semantics.
2026-03-07: Built tolerant validation mode and dataclass adapter. Early perf regressions found when full strict validation is enabled; added config knob to skip strict path in streaming mode.

2026-03-10: Added pause/resume API for consumer backpressure; integration tests started against a flaky-net shim. Identified one edge case where nested optional arrays cause delayed strict-pass failures—investigating fix.
2026-03-12: Draft PR opened for review: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1478. Coverage at ~78% for new helpers. Requesting review from @eng-runtime and @devx.
notes_for_reviewers: Please focus review on: (1) correctness of resume semantics under concurrent partial deliveries, (2) safety of auto-coercion rules in the compatibility helpers, and (3) telemetry payloads to ensure no PII is emitted by default.
Benchmark scripts are under tools/benchmarks/stream-validate and include reproducible instructions. Aim to review perf knobs before landing.
